name: modbus-fake
experiment:
# Modbus master over the modbus plugin (RTU or TCP).
#
# The default run uses the plugin's in-process SYNTHETIC slave, so it needs no
# device. Its register values are generated, not measured:
#
#   HWLAB_MODBUS_FAKE=1 hwlab run --yes examples/modbus-fake.yaml
#
# For a real device (UNVALIDATED: the Modbus stack was written from the public
# specification and has only run against its own simulator; no Modbus device
# was available):
#
#   export HWLAB_MODBUS_HOSTS="meter=tcp://192.168.1.60:502,rs485=rtu:/dev/ttyUSB0@19200:8E1"
#   hwlab devices                                  # modbus/meter, modbus/rs485
#   hwlab invoke modbus/meter Modbus.read_holding_registers '{"address":0,"quantity":2}'
#
# and replace `device:` below. Writes are CONFIRM operations and need --yes;
# polls in a capture are read-only by design.
name: modbus-fake
duration: 3s

devices:
  plc:
    plugin: modbus
    device: fake-modbus
    unit: 1
    polls:
      - {name: regs,  function: read_holding_registers, address: 0,  quantity: 3, interval_ms: 500}
      - {name: temp,  function: read_holding_registers, address: 10, quantity: 2, interval_ms: 500, as: f32}
      - {name: count, function: read_input_registers,   address: 0,  quantity: 1, interval_ms: 700}

steps:
  - {name: read-coils, at: 200ms,  device: plc, call: Modbus.read_coils, args: {address: 0, quantity: 4}}
  - {name: write-reg,  at: 1200ms, device: plc, call: Modbus.write_register, args: {address: 4, value: 777}}
  - {name: bad-addr,   at: 1700ms, device: plc, call: Modbus.read_holding_registers, args: {address: 9000, quantity: 1}}   # exception: recorded as a failed step, not fatal

clock.source: host clock (synthetic slave on an in-memory link: no real bus)
clock.note: SYNTHETIC; times only order the events
